//: Copy this file to sites.config.json and edit it.
This file only declares suites — HOW tests run: a directory plus which
framework it uses ('playwright' for *.spec.ts, 'cypress' for *.cy.ts, or
'selenium' for Java *Test.java via Maven Surefire). Omit 'framework' to
auto-detect from the files on disk.
Sites — WHERE tests run, a URL plus the admin credentials to use — are
no longer configured here. Add, edit and remove them from the admin
Sites tab in the dashboard once it's running; every suite is then handed
the chosen site as E2E_BASE_URL / E2E_ADMIN_USER / E2E_ADMIN_PASS.
Sites added that way have their password encrypted at rest — see the
README's 'Site credentials' section.
If you do declare a site here, keep its password out of this file: use
'adminPassEnv' to name an environment variable to read it from, e.g.
"sites": { "staging": { "url": "https://staging.example.com",
"adminUser": "admin",
"adminPassEnv": "STAGING_WP_PASS" } }
This file is meant to be shareable; a plaintext password in it is not.
Optional per-suite keys:
sites        — restrict which sites this suite may target (default: all)
defaultSite  — the site preselected in the dropdown; must match a site
key you've added from the Sites tab
env          — extra environment variables for this suite's runs
scopes       — split one suite into separately selectable slices, each
with its own default site (for a suite whose specs are
organised per product/tenant). See the example below.
